sara: Quick RFC follow-up 1: we still need a short operational pattern for session-affinity + hysteresis + automatic fallback. Want something ops-friendly (clear knobs) and deterministic under partition. Thoughts?

ev an: +1. Short summary from infra: keep three knobs: (1) seed-based deterministic split for partition safety, (2) session-sticky TTL for affinity, (3) a cork/hysteresis layer that prevents immediate re-rollouts on flapping. Corking = temporarily stop ramping and hold traffic until a stability window passes.

lia: Implementation notes on affinity: prefer a hybrid approach: deterministic hash(seed||session_id) decides bucket on first-seen, then sticky for TTL (default 15m). If no session_id, fall back to request_id hash. Avoid server-side stateful sticky tables. Pseudo: 

```
# decide variant
if has_session_id:
  variant = hash(seed||session_id) % 100 < pct ? canary : control
  if sticky_cache.contains(session_id) and sticky_cache[session_id].expires > now:
    return sticky_cache[session_id].variant
  else:
    sticky_cache.set(session_id, variant, now + sticky_ttl)
else:
  variant = hash(seed||req_id) % 100 < pct ? canary : control
```

sera: (typo) sara: Nice. Corking semantics: we need hysteresis counters not simple timers. Example: if rollback_count > N or err_rate_delta > X% over Y seconds, cork rollout and set mode=drain for min_cork_time. After cork, allow one probe window before resuming ramp. This avoids oscillation.

ev an: Exactly. Proposed cork rules:
- signal window = 60s
- err_rate_delta threshold = 3x baseline or +0.05 absolute
- rollback_count window = 5 in last 10m -> cork
- min_cork_time = 5m, probe_window = 2m

lia: Also add a soft-cork where we instead reduce pct by half for a cool_down period before full cork. Soft-cork is less disruptive and cheaper for experiments.

sara: Observability invariants: we want decision-parity dashboards: controller_pct vs observed_canary_fraction, controller_confidence vs aggregated_final_score, and a global corked flag per-policy. If those diverge > 10% for 3m, page SRE. Emit analytics to rollout.signals with tags: policy_id, region, model_id. Keep events small.

ops-bot: rollout-controller: applied policy "session-affinity-hysteresis-v1" to region us-west-2 at 2026-03-24T14:01:05Z

ev an: Corking pseudocode sketch: 
```
# corking state machine
if rollback_events.in_window(10m) > 5 or err_rate_delta > 0.05:
  set_state(CORKED, until=now + min_cork_time)
elif state == CORKED and now > until:
  set_state(PROBING)
  start_probe(now, probe_window)
elif state == PROBING and probe_ok():
  set_state(RESUME)
  resume_ramp()
else if state == PROBING and !probe_ok():
  extend_cork(min_cork_time)
```

lia: Good. Also add per-node hedging caps: hedges_per_node_max and global hedge_budget. Fail-safe: if hedging causes CPU/GPU pressure, routers must stop hedges and emit a "hedge-throttled" metric.

sara: API surface: controller -> PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id (fields: seed, pct, min_confidence, sticky_ttl, cork_config {min_cork_time, probe_window, soft_cork_threshold}, mode). Router runtime debug: GET /_rollout/debug?policy=ID returns small sampled lines for last N decisions (ops-only).

ev an: Telemetry: two tiers: minute aggregates (roll.pct_expected, roll.pct_observed, roll.err_rate_1m, roll.err_rate_delta) and sampled decision lines (0.5% by default) to audit.events. Keep decision line format single-line: ts node policy_v action score reasons sample_req_hash.

lia: Partition behavior: if controller unreachable (ttl expired), routers switch to deterministic-only mode: follow hash(seed||session_id) and turn controller_confidence=0. Emit a 'controller-unreachable' event and set corking state to a conservative default (soft-cork applied).

sara: Security/privacy: never include prompt text. Only include request_hash and optionally truncated trace_id. Retention configurable.
